REVIEW

items.title: 169 Mercer Street, Unit PH
items.description: Fresh off a newly completed top-to-bottom renovation, the Penthouse at 169 Mercer Street is an impeccably designed loft on one of SoHo's best blocks. Boasting three exposures and a large skylight, this top floor residence spans over 2,300 square feet and includes two bedroom, a home office, two bathrooms, a gas fireplace, and direct keyed elevator access. Upon entering the home, it's immediately apparent the care taken when designing the loft. The herringbone oak floors lead you from the keyed elevator, past the large home office, to the great room, where a large skylight provides all-day light. The heart of the home, here you have a gas fireplace with brand new green quartzite mantle, multiple dedicated seating areas, formal dining for 8, and a brand new eat-in kitchen. The kitchen was fully overhauled from its previous iteration: the cabinetry, high-end appliances, zellige subway tiling, fixtures, and leather-finish granite countertops are all newly completed. The primary bedroom suite occupies the west end of the home. Located on the corner, with views that clear the adjacent buildings, the bedroom is grand and bright. It's a true suite, with a walk-in closet, en-suite bathroom, and a standalone sitting area. Here, the views extend far to the west and south, all the way down to the Freedom Tower. The en-suite bathroom is moody and inviting, with different stone motifs throughout to create texture and drama, including polished marble walls, a black leather granite and ultra-honed basalt tiles. The secondary bedroom is located on the east end of the apartment, with large windows overlooking Mercer Street and a walk-in closet. A second full bathroom, also newly renovated, is across the hall; this time, the stone selection is bright and warm, complementing the wood in the vanity. There is also a washer/dryer in this bathroom. Completing the home is a smart temperature control system; built-in surround sound; and a large deeded storage unit in the basement. The Annapurna at 169 Mercer Street is a boutique, 6-unit co-operative on one of SoHo's most iconic blocks. The historic building dates back to 1896. Today, Mercer Street is the home to many of New York City's most exciting galleries, hotels, restaurants, and luxury retail experiences.

items.title: Open House - 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM
items.description: Chic, impeccably gut-renovated, 2 BD | 2 BA loft conversion with high ceilings, in-unit W/D, and charming details. This boutique, elevator coop is perfectly located at the nexus of Greenwich Village, East Village and Noho and offers residents a full-time doorman. Details include: • Expansive living/ dining space with three oversized windows, designated dining alcove and an adjacent foyer with a sizable coat-closet • Pristine, open-concept island kitchen with elevated finishes, double-height cabinetry and premium stainless steel appliances • Bright, corner primary bedroom with North & East exposures and a convenient ensuite bathroom • Substantial second bedroom with two windows and great closet space. • Designed by Orley Interiors, B204 underwent a complete renovation in 2026. Seller upgrades include new solid oak flooring, completely renovated bathrooms, re-configured and refinished kitchen, electrical upgrades and the addition of a mini-split HVAC system. Snug Harbor Owners' Corp is a unique collection of three pre-war industrial loft buildings and a charming interior courtyard that were converted to a 63-unit residential cooperative in 1979. The land under these buildings was originally a minor portion of the vast, 21 acre Greenwich Village estate of Captain Robert Richard Randall, knows as 'Minto Farm.' As Randall had no heirs, the farm was earmarked in his will to become the Sailors Snug Harbor Marine Hospital upon his death in 1801. Under advisement of the charity's trust, eight commercial/ manufacturing buildings were later constructed on the land at the turn of the 19th Century. Amongst them were 297 -303 Mercer Street, 258-260 Greene Street and 262 Greene Street which would later become the Snug Harbor Owners. Corp. 297-303 Mercer Street was home to a diverse set of businesses including a furrier, a young men's clothing company and a panama hat manufacturer before becoming the established doorman co-op it is today. Snug Harbor allows pied-a-terre, guarantors, co-purchasing & gifting all on a case-by-case basis. Subletting is allowed for a single year with the option to renew for an additional year at the Board's discretion. A 10% maintenance fee applies. Please note that there is a flip tax of 2% gross sales price, paid by Seller. 75% financing allowed. Pet friendly In the immediate vicinity you'll find many of New York City’s most exciting restaurants, great shopping, countless fitness options and, for the home chef, the Union Square Farmers Market. Convenient access to the 6, L, N/Q/R, 4/5, F/M and PATH will take you anywhere else in the city and beyond.

items.title: 719 Greenwich Street, Unit PH
items.description: Never before available, the Penthouse at 719 Greenwich Street offers a rare opportunity to create one of the West Village’s most distinctive residences, combining extraordinary architectural character, privacy, history, and quintessential downtown living. Encompassing approximately 3,060 square feet with an additional 1,100 square feet of outdoor space, the penthouse, with direct light coming in from all four sides, is distinguished by a remarkable rooftop setting unlike anything typically found downtown, with protected views over the West Village Historic District. A custom metal and natural wood staircase, featuring subtle nautical references that reflect the longtime owner’s life as a dedicated sailor, ascends to a charming Maine-inspired cottage and covered porch perched high above the surrounding rooftops. Beyond, the expansive private roof garden enjoys spectacular, direct unobstructed views North to Hudson Yards and the Empire State Building, along with other skyscrapers, East past the Jefferson Market Library, and South to One World Trade Center. The indoor-outdoor setting allows for use well beyond the warmer months, creating a singular backdrop for year-round dining and entertaining against the city skyline. Inside, historic character abounds with original wooden structural columns, girders, and exposed brick throughout the loft-like living spaces, with 10.5-foot ceilings and a wood-burning fireplace clad in reclaimed granite pavers that once lined the neighborhood's blocks. Currently, it is comprised of four bedrooms - a corner primary suite, two guest bedrooms (one used as an office), and a cozy mezzanine sleeping loft - along with a separate office/workshop. The floor plate offers fantastic scale and flexibility, with endless renovation possibilities suited to your specific needs. The property also has a remarkable cultural history. The penthouse was featured in Woody Allen’s film Manhattan Murder Mystery and photographed by acclaimed National Geographic photographer George Steinmetz, known for his extraordinary aerial studies, for Gothamist. The rooftop meadow is the featured centerfold in National Geographic’s May 2009 issue focusing on green roofs around the world. Originally constructed in 1909 as a book depository, 719 Greenwich Street is a distinctive 12-unit pre-war loft building with a historic brick façade and an intimate scale. Set on a quiet, tree-lined block between Charles and Perry Streets, it sits moments from Hudson River Park and amidst the restaurants, shops, galleries, and cultural institutions that define the West Village.

items.title: 111 Barrow Street, Unit 6C
items.description: Welcome to 6C at 111 Barrow, an approx 1,650 sq ft bright 2 bedroom/2 bath co-op with 12-foot beamed ceilings, a huge dramatic living room with oversized windows framing stunning open north and east views, and a unique brick fireplace. Seize this opportunity to create your dream apartment in the heart of the West Village in a prewar full-service co-op. Arrive to the large entry foyer which seamlessly leads to the kitchen, enabling it to double as a dining area. The primary suite benefits from a wall of east-facing windows providing glorious light and open city views, along with an en-suite bath and a wall of closets. The well proportioned second bedroom, also east-facing and bright, has a hall bath nearby. Perfectly situated on a tranquil, tree-lined block down the street from Hudson River Park, 111 Barrow is a full-service prewar co-op with a beautifully landscaped roof deck with panoramic skyline views, 24 hour doorman, live-in resident manager, laundry on every floor, storage and bike room. There is world class dining within blocks at Via Carota, Osteria Carlina, and Little Owl, to name a few. Nearby are all of the charming cafes and shops the West Village is known for. This is a UCC Article 9 foreclosure auction, not a voluntary sale, and the purchase is "as-is" with no representations or warranties. The sale is not contingent on financing, the buyer is responsible for a 2% flip tax, and pied a terres are not allowed. Auction terms and conditions (including deposit requirements, closing timeline, and buyer’s premium, if any) will be provided to interested parties upon written request.

items.title: 118 Suffolk Street, Unit 1B
items.description: Private outdoor space, duplex living, and a piece of New York pop culture history come together at 118 Suffolk Street, a one-bedroom duplex in the former townhouse of Baby Jane Holzer, the Andy Warhol superstar and icon of 1960s downtown Manhattan. Step outside to your own 11x15 private patio, a true rarity on the Lower East Side. Ivy-covered exposed brick, TimberTech Walnut Grove decking, and dusk-to-dawn lanterns create a quiet garden retreat for morning coffee, dinner outdoors, or unwinding after a night out on Orchard Street. Inside, the living room pairs exposed brick with a decorative fireplace and layered, designer lighting that gives the home a warm, intimate, gallery-like feel day and night. The renovated kitchen features custom walnut-stained cabinetry, Silestone countertops, a Verona range, a Blomberg stainless refrigerator, and a Monogram dishwasher. The lower-level bedroom is a true sanctuary, tucked away from street noise, with a custom 10-foot Elfa closet system. The bathroom is finished in Porcelanosa Firenze Nacar tile with a floating vanity and double medicine cabinet. A washer and dryer sits just outside the lower-level door. Low monthly [maintenance/common charges] make this a standout value in one of Manhattan's most in-demand neighborhoods. Location: 118 Suffolk Street sits in the heart of the Lower East Side, steps from Essex Market, Katz's Delicatessen, Russ & Daughters, the Tenement Museum, and the galleries, restaurants, and nightlife of Orchard, Ludlow, and Rivington Streets. The Delancey St–Essex St subway station (F, J, M, Z) is a short walk away. Schedule a private showing today and see this one-of-a-kind Lower East Side home in person. Quick facts Outdoor space: 11x15 private patio In-unit/adjacent laundry: washer and dryer

items.title: Open House - 11:30 AM - 1:00 PM
items.description: Set on one of the prettiest blocks on the West Side, this six-room pre-war home is full of charm and filled with sunlight, with leafy tree-top views. A generous foyer greets you with abundant storage. The living room has both north and east exposures and fills with natural light throughout the day. The updated kitchen is spacious and keeps its original character, including custom tile work, and includes a vented washer/dryer, a rare convenience. The formal dining room is ideal for entertaining and can easily become a large third bedroom. There are two large bedrooms plus a den, offering flexibility for a home office, guest room or library. Two bathrooms complete the layout. Beautifully preserved, the apartment retains its original pre-war details in immaculate condition, offering a rare chance to own a classic West Side home. 314 W 77th St is a beautiful prewar Co-Op Building. Residents enjoy a live-in super, a keyed elevator, bike storage, an on-site laundry room, and a landscaped rooftop terrace with sweeping views of the city and the Hudson. Washer/dryers are allowed with board approval. With Riverside Park and Central Park both nearby and several subway and bus lines close at hand, this is quintessential Upper West Side living.

items.title: Open House - 11:00 AM - 12:00 PM
items.description: Welcome to The Artist’s Enclave, a rare top-floor one-bedroom condo with nearly two centuries of New York history. Then: In 1932, a 20-year-old Jackson Pollock moved into 46 Carmine, with his brother Charles while they studied under Thomas Hart Benton. This was Pollock’s home and studio before he became Pollock: young, experimenting, and still finding his way. Now: After generations of owners, the home has been carefully updated, preserving the character and eccentricities that have always defined it. On the top floor of an 1827 Federal-style townhouse between Bedford and Bleecker, this home sits just above the surrounding low-rise buildings. Inside, it feels like an urban treehouse, with treetop outlooks and light pouring in through the skylights. Fourteen-foot ceilings, exposed beams, and a thoughtful renovation give the home a sense of openness and character, while split-system air conditioning and hidden storage throughout add modern functionality. The kitchen is both functional and beautifully updated with new appliances, while the thoughtfully renovated bathroom brings a fresh, contemporary feel. The bedroom offers a generous walk-in closet, and upstairs, a loft makes an ideal studio, home office, or creative retreat. A decorative fireplace and exposed brick bring warmth and history to the living area. Out back, a shared garden with a grill offers a quiet patch of green tucked away from the city. Like the Village itself, 46 Carmine has been reinventing itself for nearly 200 years. A milliner sold hats and bonnets downstairs in the 1850s, artists lived and worked here in the 1930s, and in 2010, the building was landmarked as part of the Greenwich Village Historic District. Its latest renovation continues that tradition by layering contemporary design over the home's original materials. Outside your door, the West Village remains one of New York’s great creative neighborhoods. Within a few blocks are some of the city’s most iconic jazz clubs, comedy venues, indie theaters and cinemas, and restaurants that have helped make the Village a destination for generations. Pollock came here to figure out who he was going to be. The neighborhood is still very good at that.

items.title: 1 Bond Street, Unit 3D
items.description: Loft living in a true New York landmark. One Bond Street, the 1880 Robbins & Appleton Building, pairs a celebrated cast-iron facade with condominium ownership in NoHo. Currently configured as an oversized 1,600-square-foot one-bedroom, this loft offers the space and flexibility to add rooms and a second bathroom. The layout is made for large-scale entertaining, with 11.5-foot ceilings, oversized new landmark-approved windows, and an open 26' x 30' great room. The open retro kitchen is highly functional and outfitted with modern appliances. The bedroom is exceptionally generous at 19' x 16', with a large walk-in closet and a spacious bathroom featuring a stall shower and a separate bathtub. Additional highlights include custom lighting throughout, a second large walk-in closet, central air conditioning, and a large private storage locker. A washer/dryer may be installed in the unit. In the meantime, a large laundry room sits on the same floor, just outside the apartment door. The Robbins & Appleton Building features an ornate cast-iron facade and a striking blue mansard roof. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1982 and converted to condominiums in 1987. Today, the 18-unit condominium offers an on-site superintendent and a video intercom.

items.title: 12 West 72nd Street, Unit 5L
items.description: Welcome home to this charming studio at The Oliver Cromwell, ideally located just half a block from Central Park. A gracious entry foyer leads into a thoughtfully laid-out home with beautiful hardwood floors, soaring 9-foot ceilings, and a separate kitchen with marble countertops. The spacious living area features a western-facing window, while the generously sized walk-in closet provides exceptional storage. Tucked away in a peaceful setting, the apartment is truly pin-drop quiet, yet perfectly positioned to enjoy all that the Upper West Side has to offer, with Central Park, neighborhood shops, restaurants, and transportation just moments away. The Oliver Cromwell is a full-service co-op offering a 24-hour doorman, live-in superintendent, central laundry, storage, and bike room. With its prime location and array of amenities, the building offers a comfortable and convenient Upper West Side lifestyle. Co-purchasing, Pied-a-terres and pets allowed.

items.title: 505 West End Avenue, Unit 12C
items.description: Select photos have been virtually staged. Welcome to Apartment 12C at 505 West End Avenue, a gracious Classic Six in a well-established boutique cooperative on the coveted corner of West End Avenue and 84th Street. The sought-after C line is known for its exceptional proportions and flexible layout. A welcoming entry foyer seamlessly blends into the formal dining room and spacious living room. Designed for today's evolving lifestyles, the Classic Six floor plan offers exceptional renovation potential. Whether your vision includes a third bedroom, an expanded chef's kitchen, an additional bathroom, or reimagined entertaining spaces, the flexible layout provides endless possibilities to create a home tailored to your needs.p Built circa 1922, the home retains timeless prewar character with soaring ceilings, original oak hardwood floors, classic moldings, and generously proportioned rooms. The apartment features two windowed full bathrooms, including a hall bath with a tub and a second bath with a shower adjoining the staff room, making it ideal as a guest suite, home office, or additional bedroom. The windowed kitchen offers tremendous potential for a custom renovation, providing the perfect opportunity to create your ideal chef's kitchen. Residents of 505 West End Avenue enjoy the convenience of a full-time doorman, live-in superintendent, fitness center, media room, laundry facilities, and a beautifully landscaped roof deck offering sweeping city, river, and skyline views. The cooperative is pet-friendly and permits in-unit washer/dryers with board approval. Ideally situated moments from both Central Park and Riverside Park, the building is surrounded by the very best of the Upper West Side, including renowned restaurants, neighborhood boutiques, gourmet markets, and convenient transportation.

About Jeff
Jeff is the Sales Manger for the COMPASS Denver Tech Center Office, where he manages over 175 agents serving the entire Denver Metro area.  With nearly One Billion Dollars in annual sales volume, the COMPASS DTC office, is the second largest COMPASS office in the State of Colorado.


Jeff has over 25 years of experience as a real estate professional in a variety of roles.  Following his graduation from law school, Jeff served as a real estate attorney for Holland & Hart, the largest Colorado-based law firm. He left Holland & Hart to join Quiznos, an international Denver-based franchisor, as Associate Real Estate Counsel eventually joining their senior management team as Executive Vice President and General Counsel.
